groups.title: CL57T P1 — command inputs and fault outputs
groups.status: PLANNED COMMAND / FAULT INTERFACES — electrically unqualified

rows.destination: +5_MOTION bus: DRIVER0 VCC_IO (+5 V) → 0.5 A fast branch fuse → this plus terminal (planned; not accepted)
STEP MOSFET drain; source goes to CTRL_0V. Socket STEP drives its gate through 100 ohm. Selected circuit awaits loaded qualification.
+5_MOTION bus: DRIVER0 VCC_IO (+5 V) → 0.5 A fast branch fuse → this plus terminal (planned; not accepted)
DIR MOSFET drain; source goes to CTRL_0V. Socket DIR drives its gate through 100 ohm. Selected circuit awaits loaded qualification.
Leave unconnected in the current command plan
ALM → selected drive relay A2. COM− → isolated alarm supply −Vo / ALARM_0V. A1 → fused isolated +23 V. Relay contacts alone feed PB1 and the diagnostic input; see alarm circuit.
Leave unconnected; no brake circuit is assigned

notes: The command supply is now selected: one DRIVER0 VCC_IO (+5 V) takeoff through a 0.5 A fast fuse to +5_MOTION; DRIVER0 logic GND to CTRL_0V. J68 USB-power jumper stays removed in cabinet operation. The interface is not electrically qualified; construction and acceptance remain unfinished.

The fuse limits overcurrent; it is not overvoltage protection or isolation. +5_MOTION is not P2 encoder VCC, P4 motor power, or the separate alarm-side supply/COM− return. Do not bridge those domains.

Raw STM32 GPIO is 3.3 V; the Octopus Pro v1.1 STEP/DIR driver-socket outputs use nominal 5 V buffers. These are different points. The planned drive interface still requires loaded voltage/current, polarity, timing and power-transition qualification; a nominal voltage alone does not approve direct drive wiring.
S3 selects command-signal voltage. The +5V command plan requires verified S3=5V; S3 is unrelated to P4 motor-bus voltage.

ALM/COM− are transistor outputs driving selected relay coils, not dry contacts. Do not series-chain raw outputs into PB1 or connect them directly to Octopus GPIO. Alarm polarity and power/cable-loss supervision still require proof.
No ENA connection does not mean that an energized motor is mechanically safe.

groups.title: Factory MR1 home harness — shared Y2/Z reference
groups.status: STOCK REFERENCE ONLY — NOT AN OCTOPUS PLUG-IN MAP

rows.destination: Original shared Y2/Z input; series switches reported

notes: Langmuir’s representative confirms shared Y2/Z indication. The physical series connection and four-conductor pin/color list come from firsthand owner troubleshooting, not a manufacturer pinout.
Four stock conductors are common + X + Y1 + combined Y2/Z. They do not provide four independent switch signals.
The owner was diagnosing a faulty molded junction. Verify every installed conductor and switch; do not reproduce that reported fault or assume the colors match.
Do not connect the stock +5V common or powered harness directly to Octopus limit GPIOs.

notes: This direct-contact option applies only after each isolated switch is proved to be a passive normally-closed contact, with no LED, sensor electronics or external supply remaining in circuit. Otherwise retain a separately qualified interface; do not treat a powered sensor as a bare switch.
Split the stock shared Y2/Z circuit into separate signals and trace the whole replacement harness. Four signals plus their return cannot be obtained by merely relabeling the stock four conductors.
